tagline: Off the mountain, through Pot Town, to where the forks meet.
intro: Route 55 comes down out of the George Washington National Forest to Star Tannery on Cedar Creek, rounds the north end of Little North Mountain at Wheatfield and turns south through Lebanon Church and Clary into Strasburg.

East of town it swings through an S-curve over the North Fork of the Shenandoah, passes under Signal Knob at the north end of Massanutten Mountain and crosses Passage Creek. At Riverton, on the edge of Front Royal, the North Fork and the South Fork come together and make the Shenandoah.

moments.title: Strasburg
moments.text: Settled by German-speaking farmers and named for Strasbourg in 1761, the town became a center for earthenware and stoneware and was later nicknamed Pot Town.

moments.title: Signal Knob
moments.text: From this 2,106-foot peak above the road, Confederate signalmen watched Union movements in the valley and signaled with flags and lanterns, and a trail still climbs to the old overlook.

moments.title: Front Royal
moments.text: By the 1790s the drovers and Shenandoah boatmen coming in for a drink had earned the town at the forks a nickname: Helltown.
